label: History
value: Adrian Treleaven is the daughter of John Tremayne's daughter.
unit: Born to the daughter of schoolmaster John Tremayne, Adrian Treleaven published short stories in magazines but struggled to find the time to write a full book. Upon arriving in the area, he moved into lodgings at the Vane house, where he was immediately struck by Lorna Vane's beauty. Captain Saul, recognizing Adrian as Damaris Tremayne's grandson, lent him his treasured life-book, inspiring Adrian to spend the summer at the lighthouse writing a novel based on Saul's life story. Though deeply in love with Lorna, Adrian initially left without confessing his feelings, relying on Nell to write to him with news of her. He later returned to visit while awaiting the publication of his book, The Life Book, and declared his love to Lorna in the garden before delivering their finished book to Captain Saul.

value: Agatha Sowerby is pious.

While she acts as a dedicated caregiver and generous neighbor, she can also be severe, meddlesome, and critical of others. She harbors specific personal biases, such as opposing higher education for women, disdaining Yankees, and strictly opposing activities like drama and horse racing on moral grounds. Her habits include dressmaking, which she enjoys, and boasting about her homemade raspberry cordial. Additionally, she holds a strong personal preference regarding romantic outcomes, having wished that Nell had chosen to marry Hugh Carrow.

label: History
value: During his younger years, Ambrose was a famous dancer.
unit: During his younger years, Ambrose was a famous dancer who later took a vow during a fierce general election to refrain from cutting his hair or shaving his beard until the Liberal party won power. On a New Year's Eve at the Seven Gulls Point lighthouse, he entertained Captain Saul, Nell, Hugh, and Lorna by singing and performing a wild dance with Lorna. After the Liberals eventually secured an election victory, Ambrose shaved his beard, though Nell initially failed to recognize his newly clean-shaven face when they spoke. Soon after, Winifred announced her upcoming marriage to him. Following their marriage, Winifred consulted Ambrose when asked to take in an orphaned girl named Mary, and he agreed to adopt her.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia grew up in a family with around six girls.
unit: Aunt Euphemia grew up in a family with around six girls and was named Jamesina after her father, who tragically drowned at sea a month prior to her birth. In her youth, she routinely mocked and rejected her suitors, once advising a former suitor to wear an elastic strip to flatten his ears. She was forbidden by both her mother and her husband from owning a yellow silk dress, and she eventually received a cat named Sarah-cat as a gift from her laundress. Prior to permitting her daughter to attend university for mathematics, Aunt Euphemia personally taught her how to cook, and she later braved a personal fear of snakes to travel to India to investigate her daughter's mission field. In her later years, she moved into Tabby's Place with her two cats, Sarah-cat and Joseph, reassuring the young women living there that she would not enforce strict supervision over them. During her time at Tabby's Place, she offered guidance to Nell Harcourt on turning twenty and character growth, and she shared lighthearted conversations about her past romances with her young housemates.

value: Aunt Martha was raised in a strict, traditional manner.
unit: Aunt Martha was raised seven decades in the past in a strict, traditional manner, an approach she intended to pass on to others. After Mary Stubbs took up residence in the manse, Aunt Martha sparred with her over food. She later became bedridden, leaving the children to manage the house in her absence. On one occasion, Aunt Martha killed the children's pet rooster, Adam, to serve for dinner to a visiting minister.

value: Belinda worked as a young helper

label: History
value: Hugh Carrow spent three years living in Alberta.
unit: In his youth, Hugh Carrow spent three years living in Alberta with his ill father, during which he scarcely attended school. During a past illness, he survived a severe fever. He later married Nell, and on the eve of their wedding, he met her while she was taking a walk after visiting Obed's grave. The day after their wedding, Hugh and Nell rode in a buggy toward their new house near Seven Gulls Harbor. Upon settling in, they were welcomed by Doctor Dave, Mrs. Doctor Dave, and Captain Saul, who entertained them with stories. Shortly after their arrival, Hugh celebrated saving a patient's life overnight and eavesdropped from an adjoining room as Miss Winifred Tolley visited Nell. Hugh and Nell frequently walked around the area, visiting Captain Saul at the lighthouse, and Hugh hosted their first Christmas dinner where he carved the geese under Nell's instruction. On New Year's Eve, Hugh, Nell, and Lorna Vane walked to the lighthouse to celebrate the turning of the year with Captain Saul and Ambrose Kerr. Hugh eventually proposed buying the Varley property in the Glen to provide more space for their growing family and his medical practice, moving his family to their new home, Hollowmere. Following a three-month trip to Europe to attend a renowned medical congress in London, Hugh and Nell returned home.

Following the end of the school term, he met his unexpectedly returned father, Stephen Stanhope, who went on to marry Rosalind. Cedric remained close with Nell over the years, attending her home before her wedding day and being fondly remembered by her as a talented writer who could turn adventurous life stories into books.

unit: Clementine Ainslie's father died when she was three years old, and in her youth, she owned a pet hen and lost a young brother. At age seventeen, she exchanged vows of love with her fiancé, Martin Crawford, eighteen years prior to his death in a shipwreck. Following her mother's death, Clementine remained mostly at home and was persuaded by her sister, Harriet, to swear a solemn oath on the Bible that neither of them would ever marry. Years later, John Ashdown met Clementine in Fern Hollow, walked her home, and eventually proposed marriage to her. Though bound by her vow to Harriet, Clementine asked Ashdown for time to consider, but after Harriet refused to release her from the oath, Clementine sent him a cold written rejection that left them both heartbroken. When Lionel Fairlie later confronted Clementine, she willingly granted his request to release Harriet from her vow so her sister could marry. After Ashdown's daughter Ida visited Clementine to ask her to marry her father, Clementine sent a letter back to Ashdown.

label: Quote
value: Clementine Ainslie said: "You fashioned it with such skill. I have not witnessed a person craft a birch cup in that manner since my young brother was accustomed to making them many years in the past—prior to his death."

label: Quote
value: Clementine Ainslie said: "Discussing things provides so much relief. I am aware of that. I doubt I am capable of understanding as well as Mrs. Carrow—yet I assure you I will not laugh."

label: Quote
value: Clementine Ainslie said: "However, I would have behaved just as badly, Grace—I wouldn’t have informed him that they were burning—and I do not think I would have ever felt the slightest remorse for my bad behavior, either."

label: Quote
value: Clementine Ainslie said: "My dear, should a minister fail to act like a gentleman, we have no obligation to honor his coat-tails. I am certain I would have simply adored watching Jimmy Perry’s coat-tails catch fire. That had to be entertaining."

label: Quote
value: Clementine Ainslie said: "At no time. He holds me in contempt—and with good reason. Say nothing further about it, Harriet. I hold no resentment toward you—choose anyone you wish for a husband. However, do not interfere with my business."

label: History
value: Cressida "Cressy" Lindsay is descended from an elite and established Bluenose lineage.
unit: Descended from an elite and established Bluenose lineage, Cressida "Cressy" Lindsay first met Nell and Honora at Old St. John's Cemetery while attending Wexcombe College, and the trio quickly established a warm friendship. Cressy used her social influence to aid her friends, and after enthusiastically begging to join them as a housemate, she moved into Tabby's Place for their remaining college years. During her time at Wexcombe, she frequently discussed her various potential suitors and potential marriage with her housemates. While staying at a boardinghouse in Prospect Point, Cressy developed feelings for a young theology student named Ezra Hale, eventually accepting his marriage proposal. She remained a close confidante to Nell throughout their studies, offering comfort and advice during Nell's various romantic troubles. After graduating and marrying Ezra, Cressy later gave birth to infants.

value: Cressy Lindsay said: "No, no, my dear. Shyness is not one of the numerous faults—or good qualities—possessed by Cressida Lindsay—Cressy as a nickname. Please use Cressy for me from the start. Well then, what are your names?"

value: Cressy Lindsay said: "Provided I am able to stroll alongside Honora and Wilfred, I will attend. Such an arrangement will render the chaperone role tolerable. Your Hugh is genuinely wonderful, Nell, yet what prompts his frequent company with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Cressy Lindsay said: "See—encircling the archway above the gate, written in white lettering. ‘Tabby’s Place.’ Isn’t that hilarious? Particularly along this Avenue filled with Pinehursts, Elmwolds, and Cedarcrofts? ‘Tabby’s Place,’ no less! I absolutely love it."

label: Quote
value: Cressy Lindsay said: "It’s true that they are exceptionally sweet boys, you know. An abundance of dances, drives, and overall festivities is planned. For failing to return home alongside me during the break, Queen Nell, you will never have my forgiveness."

value: Cressy Lindsay said: "I imagine a couple of quilting bees will take place; additionally, every old busybody will discuss you, both directly and in your absence. My dear, boredom will be the death of you."

label: Personality
value: Edmund Carrow possesses an imaginative personality.
unit: Edmund Carrow possesses an imaginative, absent-minded, and somewhat theatrical personality, and he holds a deep adoration for ghost stories. He exhibits a sense of responsibility by personally assuming the fault for others. Driven by an aspiration to become a poet, he actively composes poetry and also demonstrates a capacity for praying fantastically. His personal motivations include defending his mother and Grace Ashdown from insults, fulfilling his duty to redeem his honor, traveling to the Nile to see the sphinx, and traveling to Kettlebridge to have a tooth pulled. He is deeply adverse to seeing others in pain or injured, which fills him with an overwhelming urge to run away from their sight and hearing.

label: History
value: Edmund Carrow adored poets from the moment he learned to read.
unit: From the moment he learned to read, Edmund Carrow adored poets and spent hours reading their work, even winning a school award for composing a verse. He frequently gathered with the other children in Fern Hollow, where he mused poetically, read myths, and imagined the Pied Piper leading the boys away. After Dan Coyle taunted his family, Edmund bravely challenged Dan to a fight at school; despite his dread, he fiercely defeated Dan, forcing him to retract his insults. On his way home from the fight, Edmund was praised by Mr. Ashdown for defending the honor of women before having his bruises tended to by Nell.

label: Personality
value: Grace is an outright tomboy.
unit: Grace is an outright tomboy who possesses a cheerful temperament and declines to brood over unpleasant matters. She is determined and decisive, taking immediate action once she makes up her mind, though she also exhibits impulsiveness and carelessness. While she harbors a quiet, private jealousy toward Damaris Treleaven, any fits of rage she experiences are brief. She considers becoming a missionary as a means to view India or China.

label: History
value: Grace Ashdown moved to Glen St. Agnes
unit: After moving to Glen St. Agnes with her family, Grace Ashdown quickly befriended the Carrow children at Fern Hollow. Along with her siblings, she helped shelter runaway Mary Stubbs in a barn and parsonage garret. Grace later accidentally caused a village scandal when she and Ida mistakenly beat carpets in the cemetery on a Sunday. To fix the situation, Grace interrupted a church collection to publicly defend her father, and she later rode pigs down Main Street alongside Edmund Carrow. Upon learning that parish threats to withhold financial support were putting her father's salary at risk, Grace personally confronted Lionel Fairlie, winning him over so that he restored his contributions to her father.

label: Quote
value: Grace said: "Ida, come and mix this while the table is being set by me. Should I abandon it briefly, the awful mixture is going to scorch. The time is nine thirty. Our arrival at Sunday School is going to be late."

label: Quote
value: Grace said: "Being me suits me better, as it is far more engaging. Jessie Drew manages a home as capably as her mother does, yet would you wish to share her lack of intelligence?"

label: Quote
value: Grace said: "The moment you begin to love a location, you get uprooted. I will never, ever, ever wed a minister, regardless of how wonderful he might be."

label: Quote
value: Grace said: "I feel the same way. Every one of us girls does. I intend to just stroll by without giving him any attention whatsoever. Keep your eyes on me!"

label: Quote
value: Grace said: "A point of honour is involved. Ida, do not you venture to inform a soul. Should you do so, I will refrain from ever sharing secrets with you in the future!"

label: History
value: Harcourt was born in Harborough
unit: Harcourt was born in Harborough, Nova Scotia. By the time of Dr. and Mrs. Carrow's return from a three-month trip to Europe, she had spent fourteen years living at Grey Shutters. While at Hollowmere, Nell Harcourt sat on the porch with Tabitha and discussed local gossip with visiting Winifred Tolley, including the troubled marriage of Mrs. Pettifer Miller. She also learned from Winifred and Tabitha about the chaotic household and humorous mishaps surrounding the newly arrived Presbyterian minister, John Knox Ashdown, and his four untamed children. Later, when Miss Winifred came to complain about a scandalous letter by Grace Ashdown published in the local paper, Harcourt passionately defended the Ashdown family, arguing that the town should celebrate their talents and virtues, which successfully inspired Miss Winifred to change her perspective.

label: History
value: Following her mother's death, Harriet Ainslie resided in her old home.
unit: Following her mother's death, Harriet Ainslie resided in her old home, experiencing intense despondency and suppressing her younger sister, Clementine. When John Ashdown visited their home and engaged Harriet in a lively political discussion, Harriet warned Clementine of his romantic intentions and reminded her sister of a promise she had made. As Ashdown prepared to propose, Harriet readied herself to hold Clementine to a past vow to reject him. After Clementine revealed Ashdown's proposal and begged to be released from her vow never to abandon her, Harriet steadfastly refused, compelling her sister to send Ashdown a cold written rejection. Later, after Clementine agreed to release Harriet from her own vow so that Harriet could marry Lionel Fairlie, Harriet insisted that she would not marry Lionel unless Clementine lived with them.

label: History
value: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy
unit: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy alongside Nell Harcourt and her classmates, where she spent a spring Saturday exploring the woods, named Crystal Lake, and listened to local stories. While employed at her home school, Honora later pursued further education, earning Honors in Classics at Wexcombe College. Upon arriving in Portmaris with Nell, Honora guided her to their boardinghouse and joined her in visiting Old St. John's Cemetery, where they befriended Cressida Lindsay. After deciding to lease a historic cottage called Tabby's Place for the school year, Honora and Nell successfully rented the home from Miss Tabby Linden and agreed to take in Cressy as a financial housemate. During her final year at Wexcombe, Honora continued living at Tabby's Place with her friends until graduation. She later married a foreign missionary.

value: Honora Hollis said: "it grieves me deeply, yet I fear our trip to Grey Shutters is completely off, because once Aunty’s ankle has healed, returning to Toronto will be necessary for her. Her arrival there is required by a specific day."

label: Quote
value: Honora Hollis said: “Rarely had it occurred to me that I would one day rejoice at seeing a Mott,” stated Honora while they walked across the campus, “yet I would receive Wilfred’s bulging eyes with near ecstasy. They would, if nothing else, be eyes I recognize.”

label: Quote
value: Honora Hollis said: "What we have here in this cake is what one could term an utter collapse. Furthermore, the pillow has also been destroyed. Don't ever try to convince me that Friday isn't an unpropitious day."

label: Quote
value: Honora Hollis said: "we’ve been searching for heather—though, naturally, we weren't able to locate any. I imagine the season is too far advanced."

label: History
value: During his school days, Hugh Carrow teased Nell Harcourt.
unit: During his school days, Hugh Carrow teased Nell Harcourt, prompting her to smash a slate over his head. Years later, he rescued her from a pond in his dory and offered his friendship, though she initially refused. After attending Regent's Academy and winning the Medal, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application for a teaching job in Brierley so Nell could take the position, leading the former rivals to reconcile. He later earned respect as Freshman Class president at Wexcombe College. Hugh eventually proposed to Nell, but she rejected his romantic advances to preserve their friendship, leaving him upset. After graduating with High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize, Hugh was stricken with a critical case of typhoid fever, but he survived the crisis. Following his recovery, he proposed again, and Nell happily accepted after they cleared up past misunderstandings. The two were married in a sunlit orchard and moved into a historic house in Seven Gulls Harbor, where Hugh pursued a medical career. Tragic heartbreak struck when their newborn daughter Joyce died shortly after birth, though they later welcomed a healthy baby boy named James Obed. Hugh also traveled to Montreal to facilitate a brain operation for a local man, which unmasked a long-held secret identity. Eventually, Hugh and Nell packed up their home and bade a tearful final farewell to Seven Gulls Harbor.

unit: During his school days, Hugh Carrow teased Nell Harcourt, prompting her to smash a slate over his head. Years later, he rescued her from a pond in his dory and offered his friendship, though she initially refused. After attending Regent's Academy and winning the Medal, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application for a teaching job in Brierley so Nell could take the position, leading the former rivals to reconcile. He later earned respect as Freshman Class president at Wexcombe College. Hugh eventually proposed to Nell, but she rejected his romantic advances to preserve their friendship, leaving him upset. After graduating with High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize, Hugh was stricken with a critical case of typhoid fever, but he survived the crisis. Following his recovery, he proposed again, and Nell happily accepted after they cleared up past misunderstandings. The two were married in a sunlit orchard and moved into a historic house in Seven Gulls Harbor, where Hugh pursued a medical career. Tragic heartbreak struck when their newborn daughter Joyce died shortly after birth, though they later welcomed a healthy baby boy named James Obed. Hugh also traveled to Montreal to facilitate a brain operation for a local man, which unmasked a long-held secret identity. Eventually, Hugh and Nell packed up their home and bade a tearful final farewell to Seven Gulls Harbor.

Years later, he rescued her from a pond in his dory and offered his friendship, though she initially refused. After attending Regent's Academy and winning the Medal, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application for a teaching job in Brierley so Nell could take the position, leading the former rivals to reconcile. He later earned respect as Freshman Class president at Wexcombe College. Hugh eventually proposed to Nell, but she rejected his romantic advances to preserve their friendship, leaving him upset. After graduating with High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize, Hugh was stricken with a critical case of typhoid fever, but he survived the crisis. Following his recovery, he proposed again, and Nell happily accepted after they cleared up past misunderstandings. The two were married in a sunlit orchard and moved into a historic house in Seven Gulls Harbor, where Hugh pursued a medical career. Tragic heartbreak struck when their newborn daughter Joyce died shortly after birth, though they later welcomed a healthy baby boy named James Obed. Hugh also traveled to Montreal to facilitate a brain operation for a local man, which unmasked a long-held secret identity. Eventually, Hugh and Nell packed up their home and bade a tearful final farewell to Seven Gulls Harbor.

label: Quote
value: Hugh Carrow said: "People say it’s a pleasant old town, complete with the most splendid natural park anywhere. The landscape there is supposed to be grand, from what I’ve been told."

label: Quote
value: Hugh Carrow said: "Nell, you are merely fatigued. Come along, put everything out of your mind and go for a stroll with me—a trek back through the forest past the marsh. I ought to have something to display to you there."

label: Quote
value: Hugh Carrow said: "No. It is only because of a thing I witnessed over there during spring that I know it ought to be. Hurry. We will act as if we are a pair of youngsters once more, and we will travel whichever way the wind blows."

label: History
value: Ida Ashdown's mother died.
unit: Ida Ashdown's mother died when Ida was six years old, and her family lived in Juneford before moving to Glen St. Agnes. After settling in the Glen, Ida and her siblings quickly befriended the local Carrow children over a meal at Fern Hollow. When the siblings discovered a runaway girl named Mary Stubbs hiding in an old barn, Ida comforted Mary in the parsonage garret, listening to her fears before they reconciled. Upon learning of the death of Mary's former guardian, Ida promised to pray that Mary could remain in the area, and she later personally visited Miss Winifred to ask her to take the girl in, leading to Mary's adoption. When Mary later mentioned rumors that Ida's father might remarry, Ida was left frightened and tearful.

unit: Ida Ashdown's mother died when Ida was six years old, and her family lived in Juneford before moving to Glen St. Agnes. After settling in the Glen, Ida and her siblings quickly befriended the local Carrow children over a meal at Fern Hollow. When the siblings discovered a runaway girl named Mary Stubbs hiding in an old barn, Ida comforted Mary in the parsonage garret, listening to her fears before they reconciled. Upon learning of the death of Mary's former guardian, Ida promised to pray that Mary could remain in the area, and she later personally visited Miss Winifred to ask her to take the girl in, leading to Mary's adoption. When Mary later mentioned rumors that Ida's father might remarry, Ida was left frightened and tearful.

value: Ida mixed up calendar days while their father was away.
unit: After mixing up their calendar days while their father was away, Ida and her sister Grace accidentally sparked a scandal by cleaning house and beating carpets in the cemetery on a Sunday. Following this and other missteps, the siblings joined Kit Carrow's suggested Good-Conduct Club to regulate their behavior, though Ida remained anxious about rumors regarding a stepmother. When the club chose to fast on a Sunday to punish themselves for an disruptive graveyard song, a weakened Ida fainted during the church service and had to be revived by Doctor Hugh Carrow and Mrs. Elder Clow. On another occasion, while returning from Fern Hollow at night, Ida and her siblings were terrified by what they believed to be a ghost in a garden, fleeing to Hollowmere where Clementine Ainslie helped calm them down. Seeking happiness for her father, Ida eventually visited Clementine to ask her to marry him, promising to be well-behaved, and successfully carried a letter back to her father that led toward their engagement.

label: Quote
value: Ida Ashdown said: "Yet it was placed within her heart by God to adopt you. Had He not done so, no amount of my urging her would have achieved anything."

label: Quote
value: Ida Ashdown said: “He would go to just as much effort on your behalf, Mary, I am certain,” Ida declared. “The identity of your parents is irrelevant. Simply make your request to Him—and I shall do so as well.”

label: Quote
value: Ida Ashdown said: “Oh, Mary,” uttered Ida, sliding a gentle arm across Mary’s rigid back, “do not speak in such a way. I really like you a great deal. And you cause me to feel terribly.”

label: Quote
value: Ida Ashdown said: "Oh, no, no, Mary. I feel certain that praying to the devil couldn’t be proper. Furthermore, it would be useless since he is evil. Doing so might rile him up, making him even worse."

label: Quote
value: Ida Ashdown said: "Should you become lonely, simply gaze toward our window and keep in mind that I am in there, awake, and contemplating you. Will that not offer a bit of companionship?"

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "My new home won't be distant. Our affection for one another will remain just as strong. That friendship ‘oath’ we pledged so many years ago has never been broken by us, has it?"

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Hold on until it is your turn, Miss Nell. Oh, Nell, my ear catches father walking up the stairs. Hand me my bouquet. Is my veil positioned correctly? Do I look extremely pale?"

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Naturally, there are ups and downs in married life. Expecting all things to proceed smoothly all the time is a mistake. However, Nell, I can give you my assurance that life is happy, provided your husband is the right man."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Being so tall and slight, you will resemble a complete queen wearing it. Nell, in what manner DO you remain so thin? My weight has increased even more—before long, my waist will completely disappear."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Oh, Nell—I am terribly anxious—I am unable to carry on—Nell, I am certain that I shall lose consciousness."

Her deepest desire is to be called 'mother' by her child, and she is firmly resolved to ensure his first memory of her is a pleasant one.

value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful. No other girls reside close enough for us to play together, and none of my sisters are old enough."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: “Yes,” Isolde replied, jerking her head back, “however, it is my belief that Julia Bell is not favored by him to such a high degree. I have listened to him state that he used her freckles to learn the multiplication table.”

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Really, he teases every single girl. He makes jokes about mine on account of it being so black. He has named me a crow twelve times; and prior to this, I also have not known him to offer an apology for anything."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I really believe you are unkind. What am I to do? Mr. Pidgeon is going to force me to be seated next to that dreadful Tibby Tulk—I am certain he will since no one is sitting beside her. Please return, Nell."

label: History
value: In his younger years, John Ashdown was known as Jack.
unit: In his younger years, John Ashdown was known as Jack and later lived at an ancient manse in Juneford with his late wife, Cecelia. While serving as a local minister, he became absorbed in reading German theology to the point of neglecting his children, though he firmly rejected a proposal by Mrs. Hector Twiss to adopt his daughter Ida. Shaken by accusations regarding his parenting, Ashdown began spending time with Clementine Ainslie, whom he eventually proposed to after encountering her in Fern Hollow. Clementine initially asked for time to consider, but due to a past vow made to her sister Harriet, she ultimately sent Ashdown a cold written rejection that left him heartbroken. After Ida fainted at church from self-imposed fasting, Ashdown mourned his parental shortcomings and unresolved love for Clementine, and later relented from whipping his son Rupert after seeing his late wife's eyes in the boy.

label: Personality
value: Kit Carrow is a dependable individual.
unit: Kit Carrow is a dependable and solid individual, widely regarded as the squarest boy in Glen St. Agnes, who nevertheless takes great joy in a periodic brawl and is a skilled combatant. He harbors a deep fondness for Fern Hollow, possesses a talent for imitating the calls of any wild bird or animal in Seven Gulls, and spends his evenings preparing for an entrance examination. Passionate about military life, he strongly desires to serve as a soldier and become a famous, victorious general.

Later, the neighborhood children gathered outdoors to spend time together on Kit's final night before he departed for Regent's Academy.

He also appreciates grit in others, though he expressly forbids weeping in females.

label: History
value: Lionel Fairlie had a two-year companionship with Harriet Ainslie.
unit: Following a two-year companionship with Harriet Ainslie, Lionel Fairlie deserted her in a sudden bout of resentment and hastily married Dinah Coyle out of spite. Years later, he berated Grace Ashdown when she visited his residence, but her spirited confrontation won him over, prompting him to restore his financial support for her father's salary, resume attending church once a month, and drive her home. Later, after seeing Harriet again, Lionel confronted her sister Clementine at Fern Hollow to ask that Harriet be released from a past vow so they could marry, a request Clementine granted.

label: History
value: Lorna Vane endured a history of grief and hardship from an early age.
unit: Lorna Vane endured a history of grief and hardship from an early age, being twelve years old when her brother died and fourteen when she discovered her father's hanged body following his suicide. Left with enough money for a single year at Regent's Academy, she later returned to teach at the Glen school and entered a twelve-year marriage. Lorna eventually formed a friendship with her neighbor, Nell Harcourt, visiting her home and joining group gatherings at the local lighthouse. Despite experiencing intense envy over her past tragedies, Lorna confessed her bitterness to Nell, solidifying a deep, lifelong bond between them. Lorna later fell secretly in love with author Adrian Treleaven, though she was left heartbroken when he departed after finishing a novel. Her life took a dramatic turn when she traveled to Montreal for surgery for her husband, Rufus Vane, only to discover that the man she had been living with for twelve years was actually his cousin, Laurence Vane, while the real Rufus had died years prior in Cuba. Following this revelation and Laurence's identity recovery, Lorna returned home in grief and exhaustion, supported by Nell. Adrian eventually returned to declare his love for Lorna, receiving a blessing from Captain Saul Garrick, and shared plans to purchase Nell's former cottage for their future summer holidays.

label: History
value: Lucy is a twin.
unit: As a newly orphaned twin, Lucy was brought alongside her brother Robin by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters. Shortly after arriving, Robin enticed her outside, tricks her into jumping into a pigpen, and leaves her drenched under a water pump before walking into an Aid Society meeting. Later, Robin locked Lucy inside Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse, sparking a desperate search before she was found. After Nell returned to teaching, Lucy was terrified by Mirabel Cotton's stories of family ghosts, though her long-term future at Grey Shutters was secured when a trust fund was established following Richard Farrow's death. She later survived a monstrous hail storm that devastated the area, sheltering safely with her family at home. Eventually, Lucy was forced by Robin to skip Sunday School during a day of his rebellious behavior, though she continued to grow up at Grey Shutters, later attending family meals and gathering with loved ones to celebrate Nell's wedding in the orchard.

She possesses an exceptional work ethic, devouring labor like no one else, and is known for being savagely blunt while remaining unbothered by others due to not being excessively thin-skinned. Among her many talents, she has a good ear for music, excels at playing the jew's-harp, and is a skilled cook and bread dough maker. Additionally, she can project extraordinary shadow art on walls with her long, pliable fingers and tells spine-tingling ghost stories, despite maintaining that specters actually frighten her.

label: History
value: Mary Stubbs grew up without being raised in a traditional home.
unit: Mary Stubbs grew up without being raised in a traditional home, spending two years at an asylum and attending school for four winters after being taken in by Mrs. Grimble. label: Quote
value: Mary Stubbs said: "Of course. A better deed fits a better day. Just provide me with a thread and needle, and turn your eyes away in case you get squeamish."

label: Quote
value: Mary Stubbs said: "For four winters after I arrived at Mrs. Grimble’s, I attended school, and I have no desire for more. Being constantly scolded because my homework was incomplete has made me thoroughly fed up. There was no time for me to complete homework."

label: Quote
value: Mary Stubbs said: "Cats are completely useless to me anyway. Their origin is the devil. Look at their eyes and you’ll know it’s true. Oh well, I guess if old Martha refuses, she refuses. Still, seeing fine food wasted makes me furious."

label: Quote
value: Mary Stubbs said: "Had my family merely spanked me, I would have considered it affection. Ah well, the world lacks fairness. Taking my fair portion of beatings wouldn’t bother me, yet I have received far too many."

label: Quote
value: Mary Stubbs said: "If you were aware of a few of the expressions I might utter if I chose, you would not create this much of a commotion about darn. Furthermore, you are well aware that I have not uttered a single lie since my arrival here."

unit: Ida acts as a close playmate and mentor to Mary, even helping teach her basic domestic tasks like washing plates. After Mary shares her fears of beatings and damnation, Ida comforts her in the parsonage garret, reassures her when her past threatens to catch up with her, and intervenes to help secure her adoption. Though they share a close bond, Mary occasionally frightens Ida with heavy discussions on faith and rumors of her father remarrying.

value: Mary was an orphan girl

She was ultimately discovered inside James Taylor's former hay barn in a state of actual starvation by the Ashdowns.

Her notable hair is widely described as red, fiery, ginger, auburn, or Titian, often worn in long plaits or braided, though at one point it turned green.

value: Obed Abernethy is quiet.
unit: Obed Abernethy is a quiet, reserved, and extremely shy individual who tends to be silent, bashful, and uncommunicative in social settings. He is exceptionally timid, holding a deep-seated fear of women—with the exception of Thirza and Mrs. Agatha—as well as little girls. He despises being surrounded by unfamiliar people or visiting places where he might be expected to converse, often preferring to retreat into the shadows. Despite his taciturn nature, he is a gentle, patient, and good-natured listener who appreciates talkative companions. However, he is also remarkably stubborn, possessing a habit of adopting a caprice and tenaciously clinging to his view regardless of logic or reasoning.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy was a quiet man.
unit: Obed Abernethy was a quiet, timid man who wore a thick brown beard and lived at Grey Shutters with his sister, Thirza. Driven by a desire for help on their farm, he set out to pick up a Nova Scotian orphan boy, only to discover an orphan girl named Nell waiting for him instead. Taking her into his buggy, he enjoyed her chatty company and brought her home. Although Thirza initially intended to send Nell back to the asylum, Obed quietly wished to keep her and later persuaded Nell to apologize to a neighbor after a outburst, smoothing over her stay. Over the years, he offered the young girl gentle affection and consistent support. Noticing her poor wardrobe, he enlisted help to buy fabric and have a stylish gown made for her as a Christmas surprise. When Nell took her entrance exams, Obed joined the family in proudly celebrating her top results. He also gave her his steady encouragement as she pursued her education, right up until her graduation. Tragically, upon learning that their savings bank had failed, Obed suffered a collapse and died, leaving Thirza and Nell to mourn his loss at Grey Shutters.

value: Odette Pullen is unassuming.
unit: Odette Pullen is an unassuming, hardworking, and dutiful individual who earns top marks in domestic science and possesses great culinary skills. Characterized by a steady, sensible, and pragmatic nature, she maintains a notable composure that makes her appear completely unshakeable. She is regarded as lady-like, pleasant, and unpretentious, maintaining a gentle disposition and a tranquil, rosy-faced nature that remains unsoured despite marital arguments. Though she finds teaching tedious, she initially intends to dedicate her life to pedagogy and forgo marriage forever. She later surrenders her position at the Brierley school with plans to travel West during the autumn.

label: History
value: Before starting her teaching career, Odette Pullen secured a school teaching position in Stonebridge.
unit: Before starting her teaching career, Odette Pullen secured a school teaching position in Stonebridge, having previously spent four weeks tearfully reacting to the departure of the former schoolmaster, Mr. Pidgeon. During a romantic theatrical play of Elaine, she was cast as Guinevere, and on a separate occasion, her brother saved her sash just as she nearly tumbled into the Lake of Glassy Waters while reaching for water lilies. Later, Odette arrived with her brother Barney to escort friends to a charity concert at the Pale Sands Hotel, where they shared supper and enjoyed the evening together. Before beginning her upcoming teaching term, she joined Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow to discuss their differing views on classroom discipline. On a spring Saturday, Odette spent the day exploring Crystal Lake and an abandoned garden alongside Nell, Honora, and Isolde. As a member of a local delegation from the Village Improvement Society, she accompanied Nell and Isolde to confront Judson Tibbs over his plans for commercial advertising on his fence. Later, on New Year's Eve, Odette proposed marriage to Nell on behalf of her bashful brother Barney, but reacted with cool indifference when Nell rejected the offer. Her successful work in Stonebridge earned her a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor before she eventually made plans to move West. She later visited Grey Shutters to offer her well-wishes to Nell ahead of Nell's upcoming wedding to Hugh Carrow.

Later, Odette arrived with her brother Barney to escort friends to a charity concert at the Pale Sands Hotel, where they shared supper and enjoyed the evening together. Before beginning her upcoming teaching term, she joined Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow to discuss their differing views on classroom discipline. On a spring Saturday, Odette spent the day exploring Crystal Lake and an abandoned garden alongside Nell, Honora, and Isolde. As a member of a local delegation from the Village Improvement Society, she accompanied Nell and Isolde to confront Judson Tibbs over his plans for commercial advertising on his fence. Later, on New Year's Eve, Odette proposed marriage to Nell on behalf of her bashful brother Barney, but reacted with cool indifference when Nell rejected the offer. Her successful work in Stonebridge earned her a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor before she eventually made plans to move West. She later visited Grey Shutters to offer her well-wishes to Nell ahead of Nell's upcoming wedding to Hugh Carrow.

value: Odette Pullen said: "yet I am certain I would be unable to remain motionless. Every minute or two, I would be sitting up to check my position and ensure I was not floating away too much. And Nell, you are aware that such actions would ruin the impression."

label: Quote
value: Odette Pullen said: "Would it not be lovely if a person could have three wishes fulfilled . . . or perhaps just one? What wish would you make, girls, if a wish were granted to you? My wish would be for wealth, beauty, and intelligence."

label: Quote
value: Odette Pullen said: “I formerly believed that a marriage would come about between you and Hugh,” Mrs. Gorham remarked. “If you are not cautious, Nell, every one of your suitors will slip away from you.”

label: Quote
value: Odette Pullen said: "The main thing will be to keep order and a teacher has to be a little cross to do that. If my pupils won’t do as I tell them I shall punish them."

label: Quote
value: Odette Pullen said: "I’ll give my pupils a whipping whenever they misbehave. That is the most direct and simple method to persuade them."

value: Opal Pettigrew possesses a sunny, pleasant disposition.
unit: Opal Pettigrew possesses a sunny, pleasant disposition, delights openly in the enjoyable aspects of life, and is prone to laughter, though she also tends toward sentimentality and hysteria. label: History
value: Opal Pettigrew grew up with numerous older sisters.
unit: Opal Pettigrew grew up with numerous older sisters who were quickly married off, having expressed a childhood ambition to possess dozens of suitors. In her youth, she had her warts cured using an enchanted stone from old Mary Joe, and she once hid in a hallway pantry when her sister Tabitha received a marriage proposal from Malcolm Andres. She attended school and Regent's alongside Nell Harcourt, and during a past autumn she visited Boston. After Nelson Atkins proposed to her, she returned home and composed a blistering rejection letter. During a break from college, Nell learned from Mrs. Sowerby that Opal was gravely ill with consumption. Nell visited Opal, who tearfully confessed her fear of dying and her unfulfilled desires for her life before passing away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter.

label: Personality
value: Pettifer is an exceptionally candid man.
unit: Pettifer is an exceptionally candid and occasionally impetuous man who is noted for being exacting and critical, often proving difficult to satisfy. Although generally pleasant—a trait that doubled after his remarriage—he resents being the object of pity and holds a bias against matrimony. At times, his belief that he is predestined for everlasting damnation causes him to snap at others out of cussedness.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer initially confronted Nell Harcourt after her cow escaped into his oat field
unit: Mr. Pettifer initially confronted Nell Harcourt after her cow escaped into his oat field, but when she accidentally sold his Jersey cow soon after, he generously accepted her cow in trade and hosted her for tea. Nell later sought donations from him for Brierley projects, though he turned down her request, and the two frequently debated local town matters and community figures. When young Lucy went missing, she was discovered locked inside Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. Later, a severe hail storm struck his home with lightning and killed his pet parrot, Nutmeg, leading Nell to visit and offer him comfort. During his grief, he opened up to Nell about his past marriage, his prior quarrel over the bird, and his eventual reconciliation with his wife Emily. As Nell pursued literary ambitions, Mr. Pettifer critiqued her manuscripts and encouraged her to continue writing about subjects familiar to her after she faced early magazine rejections. During a snowy Christmas holiday, he delivered mail to Grey Shutters containing news that Nell had been left a one-thousand-dollar bequest.

value: Pettifer said: "Apologies, young lady! Expressing regret will not fix what happened. You ought to walk over and view the destruction that creature caused among my oats . . . crushed them completely from the middle to the edges, young lady."

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: "He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily."

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: “Who? Mrs. Sowerby? Do not tell me that I resemble that ancient chatterbox,” Mr. Pettifer said in an annoyed manner. “I am not . . . not in the least. What is inside that box?”

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: "I do not, indeed, and I am extremely pleased with it, as well. You have my gratitude. The surface appears nice. My expectation is that it remains just as nice underneath."

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: "Listen to my suggestion, young lady, you need to assist me in consuming it. After I set the kettle to boil, a cup of tea will be enjoyed by both of us. Is that acceptable to you?"

label: Personality
value: Robin Farrow is characterized as a mischievous youth.
unit: Robin Farrow is characterized as a mischievous, rascal-like youth who frequently pulls expressions and engages in trouble, such as incessantly tormenting cats. He possesses an active inquisitiveness and curiosity, often asking questions and desiring bloodthirsty stories, while also being described as a clever lad. Despite working with enthusiasm, he can be somewhat careless and prone to forgetting, though his troubles are easily comforted by plum jam. His ambitions include reaching one hundred years of age, becoming a shopkeeper to stock candy and bananas, visiting stone gods at the lighthouse, and gaining permission to attempt managing the farm in the upcoming year.

label: History
value: Robin Farrow was brought to live at Grey Shutters.
unit: Robin Farrow, a former troublemaker, was brought to live at Grey Shutters with his twin sister, Lucy, by Thirza Abernethy after becoming an orphan. Early on, he proved prone to mischief, such as tricking Lucy into a pigpen and getting her wet under a water pump. He later locked Lucy in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse and broke down in tears when confronted, admitting he did not realize lying was wrong, which earned him a punishment of going to bed without dinner. His antics continued as he accidentally ruined lemon pies intended for guests and knocked over a shell that shattered a borrowed platter. Despite his antics, he bonded closely with Nell, seeking her comfort when he felt jealous of others or worried about her affections. Following the death of Richard Farrow, a trust fund was established for Robin and Lucy, allowing them to permanently reside at Grey Shutters. During a severe storm, Robin sheltered at home with the family as hail devastated the area. When Nell left for college, a distressed Robin questioned her departure, though he later sent her letters filled with local news and descriptions of his ongoing mischief. While Nell was away, Robin rebelled against Mrs. Sowerby's strict rules by throwing away collection money, forcing Lucy to skip Sunday School, and telling lies, but he eventually confessed his guilt to Nell. As time passed, he matured and attended Nell's orchard wedding to Hugh Carrow, later receiving an invitation from Captain Saul to visit him at the lighthouse during a festive Christmas gathering.

unit: Robin Farrow, a former troublemaker, was brought to live at Grey Shutters with his twin sister, Lucy, by Thirza Abernethy after becoming an orphan. Early on, he proved prone to mischief, such as tricking Lucy into a pigpen and getting her wet under a water pump. He later locked Lucy in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse and broke down in tears when confronted, admitting he did not realize lying was wrong, which earned him a punishment of going to bed without dinner. His antics continued as he accidentally ruined lemon pies intended for guests and knocked over a shell that shattered a borrowed platter. Despite his antics, he bonded closely with Nell, seeking her comfort when he felt jealous of others or worried about her affections. Following the death of Richard Farrow, a trust fund was established for Robin and Lucy, allowing them to permanently reside at Grey Shutters. During a severe storm, Robin sheltered at home with the family as hail devastated the area. When Nell left for college, a distressed Robin questioned her departure, though he later sent her letters filled with local news and descriptions of his ongoing mischief. While Nell was away, Robin rebelled against Mrs. Sowerby's strict rules by throwing away collection money, forcing Lucy to skip Sunday School, and telling lies, but he eventually confessed his guilt to Nell. As time passed, he matured and attended Nell's orchard wedding to Hugh Carrow, later receiving an invitation from Captain Saul to visit him at the lighthouse during a festive Christmas gathering.

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "You do not seem like the kind of lady who would lash a small boy simply because he was unable to stay motionless. Did you not find staying motionless terribly difficult when you were merely as old as I am?"

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "Thirza did the laundry yesterday . . . and Mrs. Wiggins scrubbed my skin using hard soap on the funeral day. For a single week, that suffices. Being so exceedingly clean seems pointless to me. Staying dirty is far more comfortable."

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "However, the caterpillar was so amazingly large . . . I grabbed him from the church steps right as we entered. Wasting him appeared to be a shame. Also, tell me, was it not amusing listening to that girl scream?"

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "I only carried it out for amusement. Events have been extraordinarily quiet in this place for such a long time that I believed scaring you people immensely would prove entertaining. Indeed, it turned out to be so."

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: “Why?” asked Robin, making himself comfortable and gazing upward with a tear-streaked, probing countenance. “Why is whopper not as good as falsehood? I want to know. It is an equally large word.”

label: History
value: Rosalind Penrose was considered a beauty in her youth.
unit: Rosalind Penrose was considered a beauty in her youth and was named by her father due to his love for the fragrance of lavender. Twenty-five years prior, her engagement to Stephen Stanhope ended following a prideful disagreement, leading her to withdraw from social life into the isolated Echo Cottage. After Nell and Isolde stumbled upon her cottage, Rosalind welcomed them for tea and subsequently formed a close bond with Stephen's son, Cedric. Later, when Stephen unexpectedly returned, he sent a request through Nell to visit Rosalind; upon his arrival at Echo Cottage, the former lovers embraced in the garden. Rosalind and Stephen were soon married in a garden ceremony before departing together by train. Following her wedding, she returned to visit Echo Cottage with Cedric and attended the celebrations for Nell's upcoming wedding as Mother Rosalind.

For twelve years following his death, his cousin Laurence Vane masqueraded in his place before the truth of Rufus's passing was ultimately revealed.

label: History
value: Rupert's real name is Thomas Carlyle.
unit: Rupert, whose real name was nine-year-old Thomas Carlyle, joined Tobias, Grace, and Ida in Fern Hollow for a meal of cooked trout, where they quickly became fast friends with the Carrow children. He later participated in harvesting potatoes from Evan Garrick's field, an act for which Grace took partial blame on his behalf in a local newspaper. While spending an evening at Fern Hollow, Rupert fled to Hollowmere with Grace and Ida after being terrified by what they mistook for a ghost in the Bailey garden. As punishment for running away, Tobias forced Rupert to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight in chilly rain, causing Rupert to contract double pneumonia; after a grave battle, he eventually recovered. Later, Rupert threw an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy, prompting his father to bring him to his study for a whipping, though his father relented at the last moment after seeing his late wife's eyes in the boy.

unit: Rupert, whose real name was nine-year-old Thomas Carlyle, joined Tobias, Grace, and Ida in Fern Hollow for a meal of cooked trout, where they quickly became fast friends with the Carrow children. He later participated in harvesting potatoes from Evan Garrick's field, an act for which Grace took partial blame on his behalf in a local newspaper. While spending an evening at Fern Hollow, Rupert fled to Hollowmere with Grace and Ida after being terrified by what they mistook for a ghost in the Bailey garden. As punishment for running away, Tobias forced Rupert to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight in chilly rain, causing Rupert to contract double pneumonia; after a grave battle, he eventually recovered. Later, Rupert threw an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy, prompting his father to bring him to his study for a whipping, though his father relented at the last moment after seeing his late wife's eyes in the boy.

value: Rupert said: "Moreover, it did not seem to me that any damage resulted. That her legs were jarred was unknown to me. However, my upcoming whipping will settle the matter."

label: History
value: Tabitha belongs to the Baker family.
unit: Belonging to the Baker family, Tabitha had an uncle who started as a poet before becoming a vagrant. Though she held no ill will toward men and would have willingly married, she was never courted or proposed to by any man. Working within the household, Tabitha insisted along with Hugh that Nell rest during her pregnancy and leave the household chores to her. She temporarily stepped away from her duties when her sister broke her leg, returning later to pass along local gossip. After the family relocated to Hollowmere, Tabitha remained a fixture in the household, regularly sharing local gossip with Nell Harcourt and Miss Winifred Tolley. When town gossip turned against Grace Ashdown for wearing boots without stockings to church, Tabitha rushed to the young girl's defense. She also demonstrated her bravery when the local children fled to Hollowmere after mistaking a figure in a garden for a ghost; Tabitha investigated the scene armed with a pitchfork, discovering that the phantom was simply old Mrs. Stimson looking for a lost knitting needle.

value: Tabitha said: "Enjoy yourself and refrain from stressing over the kitchen supplies. The steering is in Tabitha’s hands. Owning a dog is pointless if you bark yourself. Each morning, I will bring breakfast up to your room."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "That he remains unmarried is truly strange, because a person of his sort could win anyone just by asking. Well, perhaps he resembles me and has hitherto failed to encounter his proper match."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "Should you be unable to, I shall refrain from attending, Mrs. Doctor, dear, despite Matilda’s leg. I refuse to cause you anxiety, and to have that sweet child disturbed as a result, for all the legs in existence."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "I shall grant that they possess an abundance of original sin, yet perhaps that is for the best, since without it they could be ruined by being too sweet. I must insist, however, that playing inside a cemetery is simply unsuitable for them."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "If I believed I possessed any standing to voice an idea regarding so serious a subject as a clergyman’s wedding I would state that I believe Sarah, Elizabeth’s cousin across the harbor, would prove a superior spouse to Mr. Ashdown."

value: Thirza has a tall frame.

Her dark hair, which gradually silvered over time, has turned snow-white and is bound tightly in a firm bun at the back. Though once at risk of total blindness, her failing eyesight eventually stabilized; while her eyes will fail no further, they are unlikely to improve significantly from their current state.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters for sixty years after reaching adulthood.
unit: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters for sixty years after reaching adulthood, having spent her childhood being called a homely child by her aunt and wallpapering a spare room with the help of Obed Abernethy. When Obed brought home a young orphan girl named Nell instead of a boy, Thirza initially insisted on sending her back, though she soon sympathized with the girl's past and agreed to keep her. Despite her strict guidance and skepticism toward Nell's imaginative antics, Thirza gradually grew deeply fond of her. Over the years, Thirza mistakenly accused Nell of stealing her mother's inherited amethyst brooch before finding it caught in her own shawl, supported Nell's education after Obed's death, and agreed to take in two orphaned twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow. Facing severe vision loss, Thirza invited Mrs. Agatha Sowerby to live at Grey Shutters so Nell could attend college. Years later, after seeing Nell marry Hugh Carrow, Thirza traveled to Seven Gulls Harbor to assist during Nell's pregnancy and provided comfort when Nell's firstborn infant died.

label: History
value: Thora lived at Wayside in Coombe Road.
unit: Thora lived at Wayside in Coombe Road, where she hosted Nell Harcourt as a lodger and was courted by her long-term suitor, John Fairlie. After twenty years of courting without a proposal, Thora broke down to Nell and subsequently rejected John coldly following a prayer meeting. However, after John's mother passed away, John explained that his late mother had forced him into a secret vow not to marry while she was alive; he then proposed, and Thora agreed to marry him.

label: History
value: Tobias Corcoran bribed Judson Tibbs.
unit: Tobias Corcoran engaged in local political dealings, at one point bribing Judson Tibbs; the exchange was accidentally overheard by Nell, forcing Judson to yield to her demands to keep the bribe quiet. Later, Tobias gathered with Grace, Ida, and Rupert at Fern Hollow, where they followed the scent of cooked trout to share a meal and stories with the Carrow children. When Grace engaged in a loud struggle on the ice after standing barefoot in a snowbank, Tobias assisted Ida in pulling her to safety. Later, Grace took shared blame alongside Tobias and Rupert in a newspaper letter for harvesting potatoes from Evan Garrick's field. Following a scare over a supposed ghost, Tobias punished Rupert for running away by ordering him to sit on a tombstone in the cemetery until midnight; Rupert's subsequent exposure to the chilly rain led to a severe case of double pneumonia before he eventually recovered.

When Grace engaged in a loud struggle on the ice after standing barefoot in a snowbank, Tobias assisted Ida in pulling her to safety. Later, Grace took shared blame alongside Tobias and Rupert in a newspaper letter for harvesting potatoes from Evan Garrick's field. Following a scare over a supposed ghost, Tobias punished Rupert for running away by ordering him to sit on a tombstone in the cemetery until midnight; Rupert's subsequent exposure to the chilly rain led to a severe case of double pneumonia before he eventually recovered.

value: Tobias Corcoran said: "It is obviously difficult—however, that constitutes the penalty. Right now, I am hungry enough to consume an idol, yet do you hear me grumbling? We should focus on a different topic. Superiority over our appetites is what we must achieve."

value: Tobias Corcoran said: "If you’ll vote for Amesbury, Tibbs . . . well, I’ve a note for that pair of harrows you’ve got in the spring. I suppose you wouldn’t object to having it back, eh?"

value: Tobias Corcoran said: "Rupert holds the greatest responsibility. From what I gather, he was the first to run away. Furthermore, being a boy, he ought to have held his position so as to safeguard you girls, regardless of the peril. Isn’t that right, Rupert?"

label: History
value: Uncle Saul ran off to sea as a boy.
unit: As a boy, Uncle Saul ran off to sea soon after his parents' marriage, beginning a life spent entirely at sea until five years before settling at Seven Gulls. During his nautical career, he saved his cat, the First Mate, and discovered Rufus Vane in Havana. After retiring to Seven Gulls Point light, he welcomed Nell and Hugh to the area, frequently sharing local history and stories from his ocean-faring life. Over the years, he spent many evenings entertaining visitors like Lorna Vane, Winifred Tolley, and Ambrose Kerr at the lighthouse and during holiday gatherings. Following the death of Nell's infant daughter Joyce, Saul comforted her by revealing the story of his beloved Margaret, whom he had lost at sea over fifty years prior. When Adrian Treleaven arrived, Saul discovered the young man was the grandson of Damaris Tremayne and lent him his personal life log. Adrian spent the summer writing Saul's life story and the tale of Margaret into a book, which Saul eagerly awaited and eventually celebrated when Nell and Lorna delivered the completed volume. After contemplating his mortality and asking Nell to care for his cat after his passing, Saul gave his blessing to Adrian and Lorna's engagement. Shortly thereafter, Saul passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse with his life-book resting on his chest, having willed his collection of oddities to Little Kit.

value: Uncle Saul said: "Nephew Hector. His understanding of it matches my own. Well, now, I am truly pleased that you invited me to remain for supper. My hunger is quite strong—I ate very little for dinner today."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: "Listen, my usual way of living is royal. Up at the Glen yesterday evening, two pounds of steak were bought by me to bring back. Today, my intention was to enjoy an extraordinarily fine dinner."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: "Indeed, I fear that is the case. I really dislike it. It gives me the impression that there might be something rather unnatural concerning myself."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: “Probably—probably,” agreed Captain Saul. “That’s what I remarked to him back then. Thinking that was a great deal more reassuring. I disliked the thought of him perceiving stuff of that nature—it felt truly strange.”

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: "Those were the words he used. I recall them just as if it happened yesterday, even if I was not entirely sure what he intended to say. What is your guess about what he REALLY intended, doctor?"

label: History
value: Wilfred Mott defended Nell Harcourt's honor.
unit: In his youth, Wilfred Mott defended Nell Harcourt's honor by getting into a fight with Elias Purdy MacKinnon after Elias criticized Nell's recitations, and he previously declared to his mother that Nell was the cleverest female student in school. Having written local newspaper pieces in the past, he was infatuated with Nell when she was seventeen. Years later, Wilfred traveled by train and ferry alongside Nell and Hugh Carrow as they journeyed to Portmaris. While attending college, he joined Nell, Hugh, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay on a walk along Linden Avenue. During Nell's term at Wexcombe, Wilfred made an unpleasant proposal to her, which she did not accept.

unit: Miss Winifred Tolley spent time visiting Nell and Hugh Harcourt, offering her candid opinions on local neighbors, ministers, and parish gossip while hand-sewing baby clothing. She was familiar with the tragic history of the Vane family and shared Lorna Vane's background with Nell, later reacting with initial anger before accepting Lorna's decision to take her afflicted husband to Montreal. Following the shocking revelation that Lorna's husband was actually his cousin Laurence Vane, Winifred discussed the news with Nell and encouraged her to inform Adrian Treleaven of Lorna's freedom. After announcing her intention to marry Ambrose Kerr, Winifred wed him and later adopted a young girl named Mary Stubbs upon being approached by local children. Known for her frequent visits to Hollowmere to exchange community news with Nell and Tabitha, Winifred often voiced sharp critiques regarding the local minister's chaotic household and his children's unconventional behavior. However, after listening to Nell passionately defend the minister's talented family, Winifred was inspired to alter her perspective. In time, she also took part in local discussions regarding upcoming weddings and the minister's plans for his children.

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "She has altered considerably of late. Her laughter and jesting resemble those of a young girl, and based on what she says, I deduce she visits this place quite frequently."

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "MR. Fiske, my lone brother passed away fifteen years back, and I’ve taken on no new ones since then. Regarding my Christian faith, I trust and believe I possessed it while you were still a toddler wearing petticoats."

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "Nell, are you trying to say that the rumors I’ve been hearing are factual—that Dr. Carrow informed Lorna that Rufus can be healed, and that she intends to bring him to Montreal so he can undergo surgery?"

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "Rufus Vane received the harm that resulted in his current state during a drunken brawl. His fate is DESERVED. It was inflicted upon him as a retribution. The doctor, I don’t believe, has any right to meddle with God’s visitations."

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "Now, you don't need to call me Miss Winifred, my dear Nell. EVERYONE would have come to the identical conclusion. Should the physicians in Montreal succeed in transforming Rufus Vane into a sensible person, they are truly remarkable."

value: Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

value: Thirza presents Nell with three simple dresses.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school
unit: Thirza presents Nell with three simple dresses and refuses her request for fashionable puffed sleeves, sending her off to study Sunday school materials. chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

unit: As the women pack up Tabby's Place in preparation to leave Wexcombe, Cyril Lisle proposes to Nell Harcourt in a pavilion by the shore. She returns to her room and tearfully confesses her decision to Cressy, who initially scolds her but ultimately offers comfort.

value: Grace is furious.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XIX. POOR ADAM!
unit: Grace is furious and heartbroken after Aunt Martha slaughters her pet rooster, Adam, to serve to the visiting minister, Mr. Perry. During dinner, Grace openly dislikes Mr. Perry, who eats Adam and preaches at her. Later in the study, Grace secretly watches Mr. Perry's coat-tails catch fire from the hearth, getting revenge on him when he scorches his new coat.

unit: After being teased at school about the loss of her rooster Adam, Grace goes toward Hollowmere seeking comfort from Mrs. Carrow. Grace returns home feeling comforted and tells her father and Ida how much she loves Clementine.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
value: Grace gives her only good shoes to Zilla Marsh.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
unit: In an impulse of charity, Grace gives her only good shoes and stockings to barefoot Zilla Marsh, who quickly leaves to preserve her new possessions. Realizing she will now have to wear her hated striped stockings to church, Grace stands barefoot in a snowbank to catch a cold so she can legitimately stay home. Ida and Tobias pull Grace off the ice after a loud struggle that onlookers misinterpret as a fight, though Grace wakes up healthy the next morning still determined not to wear the stockings.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
value: Grace gives her only good shoes to Zilla Marsh.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
unit: In an impulse of charity, Grace gives her only good shoes and stockings to barefoot Zilla Marsh, who quickly leaves to preserve her new possessions. Realizing she will now have to wear her hated striped stockings to church, Grace stands barefoot in a snowbank to catch a cold so she can legitimately stay home. Ida and Tobias pull Grace off the ice after a loud struggle that onlookers misinterpret as a fight, though Grace wakes up healthy the next morning still determined not to wear the stockings.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
value: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes Ida Ashdown to faint during the church service. Doctor Hugh Carrow and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading Grace to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, John Ashdown reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for Clementine Ainslie before returning to his theological studies.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXXI. RUPERT DOES PENANCE
value: Tobias punishes Rupert
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXXI. RUPERT DOES PENANCE
unit: Tobias punishes Rupert for running away from a ghost by forcing him to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight. Rupert endures the chilly rain during his midnight vigil and subsequently falls gravely ill with double pneumonia. After a tense battle for his life, Rupert recovers with the support of the community and returns to Fern Hollow.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
value: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes Ida Ashdown to faint during the church service. Doctor Hugh Carrow and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading Grace to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, John Ashdown reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for Clementine Ainslie before returning to his theological studies.

unit: Mary Stubbs attends church with the manse children using borrowed clothes, making a scene by sticking her tongue out at a parishioner. label: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
value: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes Ida Ashdown to faint during the church service. Doctor Hugh Carrow and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading Grace to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, John Ashdown reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for Clementine Ainslie before returning to his theological studies.

unit: Tobias punishes Rupert for running away from a ghost by forcing him to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight. After a tense battle for his life, Rupert recovers with the support of the community and returns to Fern Hollow.

value: Nell suffers from a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: Suffering from a toothache, Nell loses her temper at school, accidentally causing firecrackers to detonate in the stove and later whipping Anthony Tulk for putting a mouse in her desk. Devastated by her loss of composure, she confides in Thirza at home. The next morning, Anthony surprisingly shows respect for her actions, which is later confirmed by Agatha Sowerby.

Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

value: Grace is furious
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XIX. POOR ADAM!
unit: Grace is furious and heartbroken after Aunt Martha slaughters her pet rooster, Adam, to serve to the visiting minister, Mr. Perry. During dinner, Grace openly dislikes Mr. Perry, who eats Adam and preaches at her. Later in the study, Grace secretly watches Mr. Perry's coat-tails catch fire from the hearth, getting revenge on him when he scorches his new coat.

Later in the study, Grace secretly watches Mr. Perry's coat-tails catch fire from the hearth, getting revenge on him when he scorches his new coat.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
value: Grace gives her only good shoes to Zilla Marsh.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
unit: In an impulse of charity, Grace gives her only good shoes and stockings to barefoot Zilla Marsh, who quickly leaves to preserve her new possessions. Realizing she will now have to wear her hated striped stockings to church, Grace stands barefoot in a snowbank to catch a cold so she can legitimately stay home. Ida and Tobias pull Grace off the ice after a loud struggle that onlookers misinterpret as a fight, though Grace wakes up healthy the next morning still determined not to wear the stockings.

value: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes Ida Ashdown to faint during the church service. Doctor Hugh Carrow and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading Grace to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, John Ashdown reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for Clementine Ainslie before returning to his theological studies.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE
unit: While spending a pleasant spring evening at Fern Hollow, the children share their dreams for the future until Mary Stubbs arrives and startles them with a ghost story about Henry Warren and the nearby ruined Bailey property. unit: Mary Stubbs attends church with the manse children using borrowed clothes, making a scene by sticking her tongue out at a parishioner. label: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
value: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes Ida Ashdown to faint during the church service. Doctor Hugh Carrow and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading Grace to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, John Ashdown reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for Clementine Ainslie before returning to his theological studies.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE

Tabitha returns with the news that the 'ghost' was merely old Mrs. Stimson crawling around in white sheets searching for a lost knitting needle.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
value: Grace gives her only good shoes and stockings to Zilla Marsh.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIV. A CHARITABLE IMPULSE
unit: In an impulse of charity, Grace gives her only good shoes and stockings to barefoot Zilla Marsh, who quickly leaves to preserve her new possessions. Realizing she will now have to wear her hated striped stockings to church, Grace stands barefoot in a snowbank to catch a cold so she can legitimately stay home. Ida and Tobias pull Grace off the ice after a loud struggle that onlookers misinterpret as a fight, though Grace wakes up healthy the next morning still determined not to wear the stockings.

Realizing how neglected his children are, John Ashdown reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for Clementine Ainslie before returning to his theological studies.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Good-Conduct Club decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes Ida Ashdown to faint during the church service.
